title: HTTP Server
subtitle: Serve a DuckDB connection through HTTP.
intro: Start an HTTP listener inside a DuckDB process and query it from an HTTP client. Send SQL in a POST body, receive JSON results, and keep the process running for the lifetime of the service.

reference.name: httpserve_start(host, port, auth)
reference.description: Start the in-process listener with one shared credential.

reference.name: httpserve_stop()
reference.description: Stop the listener; call start again to change settings.

reference.name: POST /
reference.description: Put SQL in the request body to execute it.

reference.name: GET /?q=…
reference.description: Pass URL-encoded SQL as a query parameter.

reference.name: default_format=JSONEachRow
reference.description: Return newline-delimited JSON objects, one per result row.

reference.name: default_format=JSONCompact
reference.description: Return metadata, row arrays and query statistics.

notes.title: Choose the authentication mode
notes.body: An auth value containing user:pass selects HTTP Basic; a shared key uses X-API-Key. An empty string disables authentication. The listener speaks HTTP: use a TLS proxy for access beyond a trusted local environment.

notes.title: Scope the DuckDB process
notes.body: Clients can submit SQL using the served connection's capabilities. Bind to localhost for development; configure DuckDB permissions and filesystem access for deployment. Read-only database access alone is not a complete SQL sandbox. Keep the process alive.
